newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ARSENAL GOING TOP A BLESSING IN DISGUISE FOR WENGER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARSENAL GOING TOP A BLESSING IN DISGUISE FOR WENGER.

text.p: Frenchman Arsene Wenger could find himself in the dubious position of taking over a team at the top of the table when he officially takes up his new position on Monday.
While delighted that his new club could be top of the table it could be a blessing in disguise because the only way for Arsenal to go after that would be down -- unless of course they won the title.

Arsenal, who have been under the watchful eye of caretaker Pat Rice, Wenger's new No.2, for the past two weeks, have not lost in the league since the second match of the season when they were beaten 2-0 at Liverpool.

Since then they have risen to third in the table and with top-placed Liverpool not playing West Ham until Sunday and second-placed Newcastle playing Aston Villa on Monday, Arsenal could feasibly be top by the time Wenger starts work on Monday if they beat Sunderland at home on Saturday.
Sunderland will be eager to exploit any weariness in the Arsenal ranks in the wake of their 3-2 defeat to Borussia Moenchengladbach in the UEFA Cup on Wednesday.

Sunderland have won their last three games -- two of them against second division Watford in the league cup -- but a 4-1 league win at Nottingham Forest underlines the threat they pose if Arsenal are not firing on all cylinders.
But a lack of goals remains Sunderland's weakness and the absence of 1.3 million pounds record signing Niall Quinn, a former Gunner, is a major blow.
Across London Chelsea boss Ruud Gullit has demanded more passion from his players against Nottingham Forest in the wake of a disappointing week.

Chelsea are reeling after last Saturday's 5-1 rout at Liverpool and Wednesday's humiliating 3-1 second leg defeat at home to second division Blackpool in the league cup even though they qualified 5-4 on aggregate.
"It's not enough to have only quality," warned Gullit. "You have to combine it with passion and the will to win the game. If you don't have passion you can't perform."
Gullit feels it is best to forget the last two games but admits his players "owe it to themselves and the crowd to perform well on Saturday."

Forest have failed to win in six league games since Kevin Campbell's hat-trick destroyed Coventry on the opening day of the season but manager Frank Clark is unlikely to rush striker Campbell back after his five-match lay-off with hamstring trouble.
Everton and Sheffield Wednesday, knocked out of the league cup by York and Oxford in midweek, meet at Goodison Park.

Joe Royle's shell-shocked side, without a win since their opening day success against Newcastle, desperately need to halt their alarming nosedive, and Wednesday could also do with a boost, having gone five games without a win after winning their opening four matches.
Middlesbrough, who suffered their first home defeat of the season against Arsenal last Saturday, have an ideal opportunity to bounce back when they tackle Southampton at The Dell.

The Saints are second from bottom and still looking for their first league win. They have lost their last three league games and eighth-placed Middlesbrough ought to be able to make up ground on the leaders and Southampton's manager Graeme Souness, a former Middlesbrough player, still looking for his first victory.

One of the traditional glamour matches of the season takes place at Old Trafford on Sunday with champions Manchester United, unbeaten after seven games, taking on injury-hit Tottenham, looking to recapture some sort of form after a miserable start to the season.
Fixtures:
Saturday: Arsenal v Sunderland; Chelsea v Nottingham Forest; Coventry v Blackburn; Derby v Wimbledon; Everton v Sheffield Wednesday; Leicester v Leeds United; Southampton v Middlesbrough
Sunday: Manchester United v Tottenham; West Ham v Liverpool
Monday: Newcastle United v Aston Villa
